steps.review: The earlier independently reviewed positive-slope two-item lemma establishes global identification of Gaussian mean and positive variance from the specified within-person moments. Cross-twin covariance is then strictly identified by the bounded-derivative Gaussian covariance identity. Positive ACE and E imply nonsingular conditional covariance. Required calibrated item moments must be identifiable at the chosen full-measure points; this is a substantive assumption, not guaranteed by observing M alone.

Independently checked Rolle induction: division by the smallest exponential leaves all zeros unchanged. For r distinct real exponents with nonzero coefficients, r distinct zeros force r-1 distinct derivative zeros; the derivative has exactly r-1 distinct exponential terms with nonzero coefficients, contradicting the induction bound r-2. Base r1 has no zeros. Grouping coincident slopes and removing zero coefficients before counting correctly handles degeneracies and the identically-zero case. No complex exponents or polynomial multipliers are assumed.

A difference of two candidate K curves has at most four exponential terms after grouping. Four distinct equality points per zygosity force each difference to vanish identically. Applying the result separately needs no support overlap. The number four is sufficient, not claimed necessary or minimal. Arbitrarily close or distant design values can make inference poorly conditioned without affecting exact injectivity.

The global functions A=2(K_MZ-K_DZ) and C=2K_DZ-K_MZ are uniquely recovered even if original A and C exponential slopes coincide; there is no unresolved permutation because both known genetic coefficients are used. At any two distinct points from one equality set, T equality yields E equality. Positivity permits logs, and the two-point affine determinant is nonzero. The same two points determine the mean coefficients. All eight common coefficients are thereby equal.

boundaries_and_limits: Binary supports are excluded from this new sufficient condition; the prior overlapping binary-level result remains separate. Failure to meet four points does not by itself prove nonidentification.

Common exact loglinear A,C,E functions and common affine mean across zygosity are essential to the extrapolation. Arbitrary smooth component functions on disjoint supports need not be identified by this argument.

Unknown calibration, missing unidentified joint item moments, conditional measurement dependence, noisy or separate-twin moderators, non-Gaussian latent models and ordinal models remain outside the theorem.
No empirical support/calibration/missingness assumptions have been independently verified by this mathematical argument.

Population injectivity does not establish finite-sample likelihood existence, at-most-one local/global maximum, posterior uniqueness, practical estimability, power, or sampler convergence. The existing no-finite-MLE all-zero example is not a multiple-maximum witness.
